newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Philips profit slumps, big charge due.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Philips profit slumps, big charge due.

text.p: Dutch electronics giant Philips Electronics NV on Thursday reported a slump in third-quarter profit and warned of a one billion guilder ($580 million) extraordinary charge in the current final quarter.
In early Amsterdam trading, Philips shares plunged 3.20 guilders or more than five percent to 53.40 after the shock news, which was much worse than market analysts had expected.
But by 0840 GMT the stock had recovered to 55.60 guilders, down 1.00 guilder on the day.
Third-quarter net profit from normal operations fell to 123 million guilders from 539 million a year ago. Analysts had expected earnings of between 240 and 360 million guilders.

Some analysts had expected Philips to make a third-quarter charge to cover continuing restructuring but new president Cor Boonstra instead gave advance warning of a one billion guilder extraordinary charge in the fourth quarter.

"Analysis of our business...demonstrates the need to accelerate planned actions for recovery. Consequently we anticipate we will recognise a charge in the fourth quarter of 1996 of approximately one billion guilders before tax," he said.
Boonstra told reporters in Eindhoven that the third-quarter business performance was "very, very disappointing".
"The anticipated recovery of sales and income has not materialised," the group said in a statement.
Analysts said they were disappointed with the poor third-quarter numbers.

"Very disappointing," said Joost van Beek at Van Meer James Capel. "When you look at the breakdown it is particularly disappointing in the lighting and semi-conductor areas. I was already quite pessimisitc but this surpasses that."
"What I'm looking for now is for them to come up with a good strategic view."
Frits de Vries at Gilissen was also downbeat.
"The outlook for the rest of the year is not all that good," he said, adding that software & services, components and lighting had shown disappointing third-quarter performances.
"Disappointment all over the place," said Corne Zandbergen, analyst at Generale Bank.

"Almost every sector is disappointing except perhaps consumer electronics. In lighting, it's disappointing to see margins under such pressure, while in components the bad result could have been expected."
"Regionally, Asia is not growing as fast as it was and that is worrying," Zandbergen said. But he added that the billion guider charge could be taken positively.
"Boonstra has again shown that he really intends to improve the whole company," he said.
Philips said income from normal operations more than halved in the first nine months of 1996 to 804 million guilders, or 2.35 guilders per share.

"In addition to the lower than expected sales growth and increasing price erosion in various markets, income was affected by unfavourable developments particularly in the semiconductor industry and in passive components, and the costs associated with our entry into the consumer communications business," it said.
Comparable sales growth for the group in the nine months was six percent versus 12 percent a year earlier. Price erosion was four percent compared with two percent in the same 1995 period.
Finance costs climbed to 684 million guilders from 600 million, reflecting the rising cost of servicing the increased debt load, the group said.
